title: Fractions represent equal parts
content: In a fraction a/b, b is the number of equal parts in one whole, and a is the number of those parts selected. The denominator tells how many equal parts make the whole; the numerator tells how many are selected.
common_misconceptions: The larger denominator always means the larger fraction.
The numerator and denominator can be compared independently.

title: Equivalent fractions
content: Multiplying or dividing the numerator and denominator by the same nonzero number keeps the value of a fraction unchanged. For example, 1/2 and 2/4 name the same quantity.
common_misconceptions: Only the numerator should be multiplied.
Fractions that look different cannot be equal.

title: Compare fractions with the same denominator
content: When two fractions have the same denominator, the pieces are the same size. The fraction with the larger numerator contains more of those equal pieces.
common_misconceptions: Compare the denominators even when they are equal.

title: Compare using a common denominator
content: To compare fractions with different denominators, rewrite them with a shared denominator. Once the denominators match, compare the numerators because the parts are the same size.
common_misconceptions: The fraction with the larger numerator is always larger.
The fraction with the larger denominator is always larger.

title: Compare using benchmark fractions
content: Benchmark values such as 0, 1/2, and 1 can help compare fractions. For example, 3/4 is greater than 1/2, while 2/5 is less than 1/2.
common_misconceptions: Every fraction with numerator 2 is less than 1/2.

title: Add fractions with the same denominator
content: When adding fractions with the same denominator, add the numerators and keep the denominator because the size of each part does not change.

title: Add fractions with different denominators
content: Before adding fractions with different denominators, rewrite them as equivalent fractions with a common denominator. Then add the numerators and keep the shared denominator.
common_misconceptions: Use a common numerator instead of a common denominator.

title: Use visual models
content: Area models and number lines make the size of fractions visible. The whole must be divided into equal parts, and the compared models must represent wholes of the same size.
common_misconceptions: Unequal pieces can represent the same denominator.
Wholes of different sizes can be compared directly.
